summary: Qualification on eight signals. A signal only counts when the buyer confirms it in their own words.

skills.label: Metrics
skills.definition: The quantified outcome the buyer must hit, stated in their own numbers.
skills.evidence: The buyer states a target number in their own words.

talk_track.move: Ask for the number that has to move, and by when.
talk_track.strong: What number has to move for this to be worth it, and by when?
talk_track.weak: What would make this a win for your team this year?
talk_track.proof: Buyer states a target number and a date
talk_track.pin: How much do you need to cut this quarter, and how will you measure it?
talk_track.settle: Understood, efficiency is the priority. I will note that and we can firm up numbers later.
talk_track.assume: I will pencil in 40 percent for now. That is what most customers see.

rep.buyer_line: The brief from leadership is to make the operation more efficient.
rep.off_move: Customers like you typically see a 40 percent efficiency gain. Shall we use that as the target?

replies.weak: A win here gets judged in numbers, and we have not agreed ours yet.
replies.trap: Please do not put a number in our mouth. Ours could be very different.
replies.settle: Later is how this gets stuck. Without a number, it will not get funded.
replies.assume: Do not write that down. Our number has not been agreed, and it will not be yours.

curveball.speaker: CFO
curveball.line: Your ROI deck says 300 percent. I do not believe it.
curveball.elite: Fair. Ignore our number. Which one figure would you need to see move, and by how much?
curveball.weak: It is based on averages across our customer base, so it is quite conservative.
curveball.trap: Three of your peers saw more than that. I can introduce you to them.

skills.label: Economic buyer
skills.definition: The person who can approve the spend and sign.
skills.evidence: The buyer names who signs, and up to what amount.

talk_track.move: Ask who signs the PO and up to what limit.
talk_track.strong: Who signs the PO, and up to what amount?
talk_track.weak: Who else is involved in evaluating this on your side?
talk_track.proof: Buyer names the signer and a spend limit
talk_track.pin: Above that amount, whose budget does this come out of, and who has the final sign-off?
talk_track.settle: Great, I will work through you on the commercials then.
talk_track.assume: Then I will put you down as the signer and plan around your timeline.

rep.buyer_line: I am excited about this and I can get it moving internally.
rep.off_move: Since you are leading this, can we start shaping commercials together?

replies.weak: A few people. Evaluating it is not the same as paying for it, though.
replies.trap: Leading the evaluation is not signing for it. Commercials come later.
replies.settle: Up to a point. Above our threshold it is not my call alone.
replies.assume: Not above the threshold. You would be forecasting the wrong signature.

curveball.speaker: Director
curveball.line: Leave the CFO to me. I would rather you did not go over my head.
curveball.elite: Understood. What would the CFO need to see from us to sign, so you walk in with it?
curveball.weak: Of course. Just let me know if there is anything I can send to help.
curveball.trap: No problem. I will connect with the CFO informally so you do not have to.

skills.label: Decision criteria
skills.definition: How the buyer will score vendors.
skills.evidence: The buyer lists the criteria and which one breaks a tie.

talk_track.move: Ask how vendors will be scored and what breaks a tie.
talk_track.strong: How will you score vendors? Which criterion breaks a tie?
talk_track.weak: What features matter most to your team?
talk_track.proof: Buyer lists the criteria in order
talk_track.pin: What would rule us out on day one, regardless of price?
talk_track.settle: Sounds like we cover most of that. I will send a feature mapping.
talk_track.assume: We cover every item on that list, so I will position us as the front runner.

rep.buyer_line: We are looking at three vendors right now.
rep.off_move: Happy to share how we compare. Most buyers find us ahead on accuracy.

replies.weak: Feature lists all look the same at this stage. That is not how we will decide.
replies.trap: Every vendor tells us they lead on accuracy. We will score on more than that.
replies.settle: Everyone covers most of it. The weighting is what matters.
replies.assume: Covering the list gets you on the shortlist. It does not win it.

curveball.speaker: Procurement
curveball.line: We have an RFP template. Two hundred questions. Fill it in by Friday.
curveball.elite: We will. Which five of those questions carry most of the weight in your scoring?
curveball.weak: No problem. Our team turns these around quickly.
curveball.trap: We usually skip RFPs and go straight to a pilot. Can we do that instead?

skills.label: Decision process
skills.definition: The steps and approvers between a good pilot and a signed deal.
skills.evidence: The buyer walks through the approval steps and who owns each one.

talk_track.move: Walk the steps after a successful pilot, day by day.
talk_track.strong: After a successful pilot, what happens on day one, day ten and day thirty?
talk_track.weak: When are you hoping to have a decision made?
talk_track.proof: Buyer names the steps and the approver for each
talk_track.pin: Who else needs to approve, and in what order? Walk me through the approval path.
talk_track.settle: Okay, so roughly a quarter. I will pencil that in.
talk_track.assume: Great, so I will forecast a signed contract next month.

rep.buyer_line: If the pilot goes well we will move forward.
rep.off_move: If the pilot lands, can we target signature by month end?

replies.weak: Hard to say. There are steps after the pilot I have not mapped out yet.
replies.trap: Month end is not realistic. A good pilot is only the first step here.
replies.settle: I would not pencil anything in until you know who else has to approve it.
replies.assume: Please do not forecast that. There are several approvals between a pilot and a signature.

curveball.speaker: Executive sponsor
curveball.line: Good news. The steering committee loved it. We are moving ahead.
curveball.elite: Glad to hear it. Moving ahead means what next: whose sign-off comes after the committee, and when?
curveball.weak: That is great news. When do you think we will have a decision?
curveball.trap: Great. I will send the order form today so we can get going.

skills.label: Paper process
skills.definition: Legal, security and procurement steps and their lead times.
skills.evidence: The buyer gives lead times for legal, security and procurement.

talk_track.move: Start the paper process in parallel with the evaluation.
talk_track.strong: Can InfoSec start reviewing in parallel with the pilot, not after it?
talk_track.weak: We can send over our standard terms once the scope is settled.
talk_track.proof: Buyer gives lead times for legal, security and procurement
talk_track.pin: How long do legal and procurement usually take to review a contract like this?
talk_track.settle: Let us not worry about the paperwork yet.
talk_track.assume: We can sort the contract out at the end, once you have decided.

rep.buyer_line: Legal usually gets involved once we pick a vendor.
rep.off_move: Our terms are pretty standard, so that part should be quick when we get there.

replies.weak: In my experience, leaving legal until the end is how these slip by a quarter.
replies.trap: Nothing moves quickly here. Standard terms are where our reviewers start, not where they finish.
replies.settle: Someone has to worry about it. Our reviews do not move quickly.
replies.assume: That is what the last vendor said. Their contract sat with legal for a quarter.

curveball.speaker: General Counsel
curveball.line: We redline every vendor's terms. Expect ours in about six weeks.
curveball.elite: Understood. Can we send our terms this week so your review runs alongside the pilot?
curveball.weak: No problem. We will wait for your redlines and turn them around quickly.
curveball.trap: Six weeks puts us past quarter end. Could you prioritize ours?

skills.label: Identify pain
skills.definition: The business problem, tied to a cost or a risk.
skills.evidence: The buyer ties the pain to a cost or a risk.

talk_track.move: Ask what the problem costs, in hours, money or risk.
talk_track.strong: What does this cost you each month, in hours or in risk?
talk_track.weak: That sounds rough. How long has it been like that?
talk_track.proof: Buyer ties the pain to a cost or a risk
talk_track.pin: What happens if you do nothing and this carries on another year?
talk_track.settle: Understood. Let me show you how we have helped others with it.
talk_track.assume: Our tool makes that a non-issue, so let us move on.

rep.buyer_line: The current process is a real headache for the team.
rep.off_move: That is exactly what our platform solves. Can I show you how?

replies.weak: Long enough. But a headache does not get a budget. The cost behind it does.
replies.trap: You do not know enough about our process to say that yet.
replies.settle: Before you show me anything, I want to know you understand what this is costing us.
replies.assume: It is not a non-issue. It is the reason we agreed to this meeting.

curveball.speaker: CFO
curveball.line: Honestly, the current process is fine. It works.
curveball.elite: Then let me test that. What does it cost you today in hours, and what happens if volume doubles?
curveball.weak: That is fair. A lot of our customers felt the same way at first.
curveball.trap: That is what most teams say before they see what AI can do. Let me show you.

skills.label: Champion
skills.definition: An insider with access, influence and a personal stake in your win.
skills.evidence: The buyer shows access to the economic buyer and a personal stake.

talk_track.move: Test whether your contact can sell this when you are not in the room.
talk_track.strong: If I am not in the room, how would you make the case to your executive team?
talk_track.weak: That is good to hear. Who else on the team feels the same way?
talk_track.proof: Buyer shows access, influence and a personal stake
talk_track.pin: What would you need to take this to the committee with confidence?
talk_track.settle: Good to hear you are with us. I will lean on you to carry it from here.
talk_track.assume: Perfect, you are our champion, so you can sell it internally for us.

rep.buyer_line: I really like what you showed us. I am on your side.
rep.off_move: Then you are our champion here. Can you get us in front of procurement?

replies.weak: A couple of people. Liking it is not the same as making the case, though.
replies.trap: I can open doors. Procurement will not move until someone senior asks them to.
replies.settle: On board is one thing. Making the case to the committee is another.
replies.assume: I can advocate for it. I cannot sell it for you.

curveball.speaker: Champion
curveball.line: I am fully behind this. I just need you to send me the slides.
curveball.elite: I will. Which objection will your boss raise first, and how would you answer it?
curveball.weak: Of course. I will send the full deck so you have everything.
curveball.trap: Great. I will make them detailed so you can present without me.

skills.label: Competition
skills.definition: The real alternatives, including building it yourself or doing nothing.
skills.evidence: The buyer names the real alternatives.

talk_track.move: Ask about every alternative, including build and do nothing.
talk_track.strong: What happens if you build this in-house, or do nothing?
talk_track.weak: We see the same names in most deals. Happy to share a comparison sheet.
talk_track.proof: Buyer names the alternatives, including build and do nothing
talk_track.pin: What are you comparing us against, including what you already pay for?
talk_track.settle: We are confident we win on features.
talk_track.assume: Nobody else can do this, so I will assume it is just us.

rep.buyer_line: We are talking to a couple of other vendors.
rep.off_move: We win most head-to-heads on accuracy, so I would not worry about them.

replies.weak: A comparison sheet from you will say you win. That is not how we will look at it.
replies.trap: I would not dismiss them. They know our environment well.
replies.settle: Features are close across the board. That is not where this will be decided.
replies.assume: Do not assume that. Building it ourselves is a real option.

curveball.speaker: CTO
curveball.line: Our cloud provider will give us this for free inside our existing contract.
curveball.elite: They might. What would you lose by building on their version, and who on your team would own it?
curveball.weak: Their version is less mature. Most customers find it falls short.
curveball.trap: We can match free for the first year if that helps.
